title: Regulation of lysosomal potassium channels
text:
Program Director/Principal Investigator (Last, First, Middle): Ren, Dejian
 Lysosomes are important to many aspects of cellular function, and dysfunction in lysosomes results in
diseases such as lysosomal storage diseases and neurodegeneration. The proposed research will determine
the molecular mechanisms by which the lysosomal potassium channel protein TMEM175 is regulated and how
the channel contributes to lysosomal function and neurodegenerative diseases. The studies will lead to
discoveries related to neurodegenerative diseases and will provide foundation for disease intervention.

title: Precision single-cell mapping of chromatin-associated protein activity by molecular footprinting to chart disruptions to gene regulation and dissect tumor heterogeneity in cancer
text:
Single cells are the fundamental unit of human biology, and understanding the mechanisms of gene regulation
at the level of the single cell is crucial for defining dysregulation in cancer, as well as for identifying new targets
for the development of more effective anti-tumor therapies. Although recently there have been incredible
advances in single-cell sequencing methods, due to technical limitations we currently lack approaches that are
capable of directly mapping all the regulatory protein factors that bind to DNA to enact gene expression programs
at the single-cell level, leaving a significant gap in our knowledge of the gene regulation landscape and how this
is altered in cancer cells. To address this challenge, here we develop high-throughput methods to map single-
cell DNA:protein interactions together with other genetic, chromatin, histone or transcriptomic features to
accurately define gene regulatory networks in single cells, which can be leveraged to chart cellular dysregulation
at unprecedented detail in human tumor cells.

title: Utilizing platelet-targeted gene therapy to induce immune tolerance in food allergy
text:
Food allergy is a significant public health and economic concern. It occurs when oral immune tolerance fails, and
currently, there is no cure for those with food allergy. In this application, we aim to develop a new approach to
induce immune tolerance for treating food allergy using platelet-targeted gene and cell therapy.

title: Multivariate genome-wide association analysis of opioid-related traits in half a million diverse individuals
text:
Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a serious public health emergency in the United States and across the globe.
Although it is clear that OUD is heritable, very few genes have been identified. We will collect detailed
information about pre-addiction traits, including opioid use and misuse in half a million research participants for
whom genotype information is also available, and will use these data to better understand how genetic
influences shape use and misuse of opioids, which will foster discoveries that can improve options for
preventing and treating OUD.

title: Non-Invasive Seizure Forecasting System Using E-Diaries, Internal and External Factors
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because seizures affect approximately 4 million people with
epilepsy in the United States. The project is relevant to the NINDS mission of reducing the burden of neurological
disease. Noninvasive forecasting of seizures could profoundly improve the quality of life, decrease injuries and
decrease mortality.

title: Mechanisms Governing Nerve-Mediated Control of Corneal Wound Healing: New Hope for Patients with Neurotrophic Keratopathy
text:
The mechanism of sensory innervation-induced regulation of limbal stem cells (LSCs) during corneal epithelial
renewal, required for corneal maintenance and wound healing and ultimately critical for vision, is unknown.
Based on preliminary findings, we hypothesize that Schwann cells (SCs) residing in the corneal limbus alongside
LSCs are critical in mediating the innervation-dependent activity of LSCs. Therefore, we propose mechanistically
defining the paracrine interactions between SCs and LSCs that regulate LSC activity, which, in turn, will enable
development of novel topical therapeutics to treat NK in human patients.

title: Enhancing endothelial cell engraftment via transplantation of exogenous mitochondria
text:
Ischemic diseases, like heart attacks, occur when blood flow to organs and tissues is blocked, leading to damage.
This project aims to develop a new method to improve the transplantation of endothelial cells by using exogenous
mitochondria, enhancing the restoration of small blood vessels in affected tissues.

title: The paradox of flavivirus antigenic non-reciprocity
text:
Pre-existing immunity to one mosquito-borne flavivirus can affect the outcome of infection with other flavivirus-
es in complex ways. We propose to integrate studies of human populations and non-human primate models to
understand how the order in which one is infected with different flaviviruses affects the immune response and
outcome of infections. Our findings will contribute to improved vaccination strategies and risk assessments of
emerging flaviviruses.

title: Opportunistic Screening for ASCVD using a Multimodal Deep Learning Risk Prediction Model
text:
Public Health Relevance
PROJECT NARRATIVE Routine chest CT examinations contain prognostic information that is
often underutilized for its value in primary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular
disease (ASCVD), leaving missed opportunities for incidental screening to predict future
cardiovascular events, such as heart attack and stroke. Current risk assessment tools,
such as Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), are poor predictors of ASCVD due to data
limitations, most notably the static nature of the data and lack of model complexity,
resulting in misestimation in younger patients with minimal comorbidities. A graph- based
multimodal fusion model that integrates imaging and electronic medical record data is
essential to addressing the data limitations of outdated tools and creating more
sophisticated technology that supports opportunistic screening of a larger population of
patients as well as earlier prevention strategies and therapeutics.

title: Editing basal cells for durable gene therapy of cystic fibrosis
text:
Here, this proposal is relevant to public health because it seeks to develop lipid nanoparticles that protect
therapeutic nucleic acids and overcome the mucus and cellular barriers to deliver therapeutic nucleic acids that
correct mutations towards treatment of genetic disease cystic fibrosis for durable therapy. The proposed work is
relevant to part of the NIH’s mission to help further understanding biological systems and leveraging that
knowledge to improve health and reduce illness.

title: Conformational Energetics and Heterogeneity to Reveal Gating Mechanisms of TRPV and TRPM Ion Channels
text:
TRPV1-2 and TRPM2 ion channels are multimodal sensors that transduce a variety of signal
modalities into electrical signals to allow cells to adapt to their changing environment. In this
proposal, we will use a combination of patch-clamp electrophysiology and fluorescence lifetime
imaging microscopy to measure the energetic coupling between the sensing modules and the
channels’ gates and among different sensing modules to explain the molecular mechanisms by
which environmental signals control the gating process.

title: Biomechanics in Regenerative Medicine (BiRM) Training Program
text:
To meet the challenges in regenerating, repairing or replacing tissues that serve a mechanical function, the
Biomechanics in Regenerative Medicine (BiRM) training program aims to provide holistic training to doctoral
students in bioengineering to excel in both biomechanics of all relevant length scales and in regenerative biology.
The combined strengths of the University of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Pittsburgh
Medical Center and the McGowan Institute for Regenerative Medicine make it a unique place for a new
generation workforce to be trained in order to meet the critical needs for improving existing as well as to develop
novel and advanced therapies in regenerative medicine.

title: Orthogonal CRISPR GEMMs
text:
This work aims to further a technology that enables the study of genetic interactions in vivo with the
goal of overcoming the one-gene-at-a-time approach to studying functional genomics in mouse models.

title: AI-based Clinical decision support to idenTify wOmeN for HIV testing and PrEP in Florida (ACTION-HIV)
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE/PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
The project proposes to develop an HIV risk prediction model (ACTION-HIV algorithm) that can detect women
with a higher risk of HIV and translate the ACTION-HIV algorithm into a clinical decision support (CDS)
platform integrated into an electronic health record (EHR) system to assess its feasibility, acceptability, and
usability. This is a major step toward overcoming the gaps in existing HIV risk prediction algorithms and
helping providers identify women for HIV testing and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Our innovative EHR-
based CDS tool is relevant to public health as it can have a potentially significant impact on increasing HIV
testing, reducing sex disparity in PrEP uptake, and decreasing new HIV infection in Florida.

title: Inflammatory cell death in systemic lupus erythematosus
text:
This project is relevant to public health because it addresses the molecular mechanisms that cause and
perpetuate systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a debilitating disease that disproportionately affects women in
their 20s to 50s. We will establish new biomarkers to quantitate inflammatory cell death pathways of
importance in SLE.

title: EMbArK: Empagliflozin Treatment of Ischemic with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries (INOCA)
text:
Ischemia with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries (INOCA) is an increasingly recognized disease caused by
coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) and endothelial dysfunction (EnD), that leads to impaired myocardial
blood flow, ischemia, and angina despite the absence of obstructive coronary disease. The goal of this is study
is to investigate the effects of sodium–glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) on CMD and EnD in INOCA
patients with CMD through a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, mechanistic clinical trial; and to
investigate the tumor necrosis factor α, nuclear factor kB, endothelin-1 (TNFα – NF-κB – ET-1) pathway on EnD
in INOCA participants with CMD, and how it is modulated by SGLT2i. We hypothesize that SGLT2i will improve
CMD; and that there is increased activation of the TNFα – NF-κB – ET-1 pathway resulting in EnD in INOCA
participants with CMD that will be disrupted by SGLT2i leading to reversal of EnD.

title: Metabolism and physiology of tissue stem cell lineages in the Drosophila ovary.
text:
Stem cells maintain the function of many of our organs and are highly influenced by
metabolism, physiology, and various stresses. We propose to take advantage of
powerful research tools in fruit flies to discover how cellular metabolic requirements
change as stem cells divide and give rise to the specialized cell types of our organs, and
how brain dopamine and other stress-related factors influence these cells. This work will
generate foundational knowledge about how stem cell lineages are regulated and
impacted by metabolic abnormalities or stresses, which will be broadly relevant to a wide
variety of organisms, including humans.

title: Myelin and non-myelin immune responses in Multiple sclerosis
text:
In this project, we will study the cross-reactivity of myelin specific CD4 T cells in Multiple sclerosis (MS) patients’
blood and cerebrospinal fluid. Additionally, we will test the cross-reactivity in transgenic model. The outcome of
our studies will have major implications for understanding MS-initiating triggers.

title: Chemoenzymatic glycan editing for deciphering biological functions of glycans
text:
RELEVANCE / PROJECT NARRATIVE
 Understanding glycan-mediated signaling, cell differentiation, activation or suppression will pave the way
for the development of glycan-centric approaches for the treatment of a wide range of human diseases. These
research efforts are closely aligned with the NIH NIGMS mission to promote glycoscience and to support the
development of tools and methods to engineer and manipulate cells to advance our understanding of
fundamental cellular principles.

title: Regulation of Myonuclear Turnover Dynamics in Multinucleated Muscle Cells
text:
Maintaining healthy skeletal muscles is crucial for health and longevity. This project aims to address a critical
gap in our understanding of skeletal muscle biology by determining the extent, and underlying mechanism, of
myonuclear turnover under resting conditions, with age or in response to exercise. This project has important
implications for the maintenance of muscle quality during the aging process, and furthermore, for the potential
long-term efficacy of gene therapy strategies for treating muscle diseases.
